articles.title: SJAA Annual Awards and Board Elections
articles.summary: The SJAA announced the results of its annual board elections and awards at its February 19th, 2022 meeting, held online due to COVID-19. Rob Jaworski, Wolf Witt, and Glenn Newell were reelected, and Steven Nelson was elected to the Board. Peter Melhus was honored with the SJAA Award for his dedicated service, and President Ken Miura announced his upcoming transition from the presidency while continuing as a director.

articles.title: Call for Volunteers and Open Positions
articles.summary: The SJAA is issuing a call for volunteers to fill open positions, including executive committee officer roles such as President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer. Additionally, the organization seeks program leaders for initiatives like Donations, QuickSTARt, School Star Party, and Armchair. Officer elections are scheduled for March 19, with a deadline of March 8 for interested members to contact the secretary.

articles.title: How Dark Matter Could Be Measured in the Solar System
articles.summary: A new study calculates how dark matter's gravity affects objects in our solar system and proposes a future experiment to directly measure its influence. Researchers predict dark matter contributes significantly to the 'galactic force' in the outer solar system, subtly altering spacecraft trajectories and potentially impacting distant comets or the hypothetical Planet 9. The proposed experiment involves a spacecraft dropping a reflective ball at 100 astronomical units to isolate and measure dark matter's gravitational pull.

articles.title: NASA Asteroid Tracking System Now Capable of Full Sky Search
articles.summary: NASA's Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System (ATLAS) has achieved full-sky search capability, becoming the first system to scan the entire dark sky every 24 hours for near-Earth objects (NEOs). This milestone was reached by expanding from two telescopes in Hawai'i to include two new observatories in South Africa and Chile, significantly enhancing planetary defense efforts. ATLAS plays a critical role in detecting potential impact hazards and complements other NASA initiatives like the DART mission and the NEO Surveyor space telescope.

articles.title: A Gallery of Celestial Objects
articles.summary: This article highlights the importance of observing celestial objects across the entire electromagnetic spectrum, showcasing how data from various telescopes, including recent missions like JWST and IXPE, are combined. It presents a gallery of cosmic objects—R Aquarii, Cassiopeia A, Guitar Nebula, and Abell 2597—to illustrate how X-ray data from NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, integrated with optical and radio observations, provides unique insights into energetic processes throughout the universe.

articles.title: Hubble Examines a Star-Forming Chamaeleon
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope imaged Chamaeleon Cloud I, a segment of the 65-light-year wide Chamaeleon Cloud Complex, revealing active star formation with dusty clouds, reflection nebulae, and Herbig-Haro objects. Hubble's observations in this region were part of a search for extremely dim, low-mass brown dwarfs, leading to the discovery of six new candidates that help astronomers understand these 'failed stars'.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is monitoring the COVID-19 situation in Santa Clara County, potentially canceling events involving close contact and shared telescope surfaces. The article also announces the reelection of three board members, the election of Steven Nelson to the board, and upcoming online officer elections for President, Vice-President, Treasurer, and Secretary. Additionally, the SJAA is seeking volunteers to resume its public outreach programs, specifically the Starry Nights Program.

articles.title: Board Meeting Excerpts and Association Announcements
articles.summary: SJAA Board Meeting excerpts from December 2021 to February 2022 highlight discussions on potential collaborations with West Valley College for meetings and star parties, along with planning for in-town public Electronically Assisted Astronomy (EAA) events and enforcing minor attendance policies. Key announcements include the addition of the 'International Observe the Moon' event to the 2022 calendar, election results for board members, Peter Meihus as the SJAA Award Winner, and Nancy Lieu as the new Volunteer Coordinator. Funds were also allocated for the solar program, and upcoming officer elections were scheduled.

articles.title: SJAA Programs and Resources
articles.summary: The article outlines various programs and resources offered by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) to engage its members and the community in astronomy. These include educational initiatives for beginners, specialized workshops and interest groups for astrophotography, telescope repair services, and opportunities for observational astronomy. Additionally, SJAA provides a library and an equipment loaner program to support astronomical learning and exploration.
